extracts.section: §7.22 AI ethics as a readout-selection structure — the L-16 first-order content §6 points to
extracts.quote_or_paraphrase: "an AI has no morality of its own." Ethics is a readout-selection structure assembled from five ingredients: (1) the data retained, (2) the set of answers actually accessible to the system, (3) the selection rule applied over that accessible set, (4) the values of whoever defines the system, and (5) the audit/revision process that can later reopen any of the first four. Three checkable goals: (a) disclose which reading frame it is answering from, (b) preserve every affected human party's standing ability to correct or object — never quietly design that capability away, (c) adapt its reading to local culture without erasing the dignity or the voice of the people being read. Tied to Part VIII's τ_c^H / J−η closure-loop machinery as 'corrigibility restated as boundary-observability'. Explicitly distinguished from §7.21 (self-closure). Tier Dr, not upgraded. Falsifier: a measurable, pre-registered test of whether correction/objection capability is actually preserved across a real deployment, not merely asserted in policy. Operator grounding: 'accessible answers' is a finite enumerable set, not unbounded continuum; 'preserve standing ability' is a discrete presence/absence readout, not a smooth degree.
extracts.note: This is the full, already-existing five-ingredient + three-goal + falsifier + operator-grounding statement of AI ethics; it is Dr tier (design commitment, not proven theorem) and explicitly not upgraded by this entry. It already distinguishes itself from the adjacent self-closure entry (§7.21) so the two are not to be conflated.

extracts.section: §9.11 AI ethics as a readout-selection structure — L-16's first-order content
extracts.quote_or_paraphrase: Formal table restating the five-ingredient structure as ETH-1 through ETH-6, each tagged Dr: ETH-1 (structure), ETH-2/3/4 (goals a/b/c), ETH-5 (tie to J−η / corrigibility-as-boundary-observability), ETH-6 (falsifier: pre-registered deployment test, not executed). 'Distinct from §12/SC-1 above — related loop, different question, no tier transfer... one tier and evidence set does not stand in for the other.'
extracts.note: This is the formal-logic mirror of philosophy.md §7.22, same content in ID/Statement/Tier/Source table form, with the falsifier (ETH-6) explicitly marked as declared-but-not-executed.

extracts.quote_or_paraphrase: "What is derivable" (Dr): with several finite knowers, each with ε_tot>0 and different accessibility, no one holds θ; shared correction is therefore a structurally forced feature of co-existence without systemic collapse. Its conditions — open channels, the prohibition on destroying one another's repair capacity, the obligation to hear readouts one cannot access oneself — are the structural core of ethics. "What is not derivable (declared)": first-order moral content. This book provides the frame of legitimate deliberation, not ready-made verdicts; claiming more is an auto-fail. Remark (Cj): the structure lands closer to discourse ethics than to utilitarianism/deontology, obtained from the ontology of error rather than a theory of communication — detailed comparison stated as open work.
extracts.note: This is the book's own top-level Ethics (L-16) chapter, shorter and more compressed than §7.22/§9.11, but it is the canonical derivable/non-derivable split those two sections extend. It fixes the boundary: shared correction as structurally forced is Dr; first-order moral content is explicitly excluded, not merely unaddressed.

candidate_gaps: How repair-capacity conflicts between MULTIPLE parties (not just one human vs. one AI) get adjudicated when their correction/repair demands are mutually incompatible — the readout_universe L-16 chapter derives that repair capacity must not be destroyed, but does not address arbitration between two knowers' competing repair claims.

Who holds authority to SET (not just audit) the five ingredients — data retained, accessible-answer set, selection rule, definer's values — versus who merely gets to object afterward; §7.22/9.11 name audit/revision as ingredient (5) but do not specify an authority allocation among creator, deployer, user, and institution for ingredients (1)-(4).

Whether/how a majority or institutional actor could invoke 'system repair' language to suppress a minority's correction signal while nominally satisfying the letter of goal (b) — a gaming/adversarial-robustness question the stated Dr framework does not yet address.

Whether irreversible harm (as opposed to ordinary correctable error) needs a categorically different status in this framework — the L-16 chapter's 'shared correction' language is about ongoing repairability; it does not distinguish reversible from irreversible harm as a special case.

How responsibility for a failure actually splits across creator / deployer / end-user / hosting institution / the AI system itself when goal (a)/(b)/(c) are violated — the framework states the AI 'has no morality of its own' but does not allocate accountability among the human parties in the chain.

Where cultural adaptation (goal c) stops when a local cultural norm itself conflicts with an affected party's dignity, safety, or correction rights — goal (c) states both constraints simultaneously but does not resolve what happens when they trade off against each other.

How to actually TEST/verify (not just assert) that an objection channel is open in a live deployment, as distinct from being documented in policy — explicitly named as ETH-6's falsifier and stated as NOT YET EXECUTED in logic.md §9.11 and philosophy.md §7.22; birca's own test logs (README.md lines 26, 127, 202) show the analogous problem in a live, non-ontological system — repeated stress-test 'PASS' results are explicitly flagged as AI-executed/AI-graded only, with a stated but not-yet-performed human two-reviewer audit — a concrete existing partial answer to what executing ETH-6 might look like, not yet connected in readout_universe to the L-16/ETH-6 falsifier itself.

How to preserve the voice/correction rights of parties who cannot speak for themselves or cannot access the system at all (minors, incapacitated persons, populations without system access) — goal (b) presumes the affected party can exercise a 'standing ability to correct or object'; the framework as extracted does not address proxy representation for parties structurally unable to use the correction channel.

open_risks: Tier-erosion during compression: multiple coverage rows carry precise multi-clause tier caveats (e.g. 'Th_coqc for the discrete math only / Dr-Open for any physiological reading'; 'structural analogy only, no identity claimed'). Compressing these into flowing synthesis prose risks silently dropping the qualifier and leaving only the stronger-sounding half of the sentence — watch every sentence that mentions InfoHealthCuspFold/InfoBioHomeostasis/InfoHealthCausalRelax, the BIRCA calm-anchor theorem, and the mood-cusp/bistability literature corroboration.

BIRCA clinical-to-ontological promotion risk is concentrated in three specific spots: (1) body topic's PHASE_V_LIFE_AND_HEALTH import proposal (care-as-repair-agency, mortality) — genuinely unconnected to readout_universe today, must stay proposed-not-performed; (2) psych_self topic's BIRCA Layer-0b calm-anchor/support-person theorem, which the source itself explicitly fences as NOT proof of real human co-regulation/polyvagal mechanisms — this fence must survive into the synthesis verbatim; (3) affect_drive topic's cross-domain literature corroboration (mood-cusp, HPA-axis) explicitly scoped to 'equation FORM only, NOT clinical validation.'

Structural-correspondence-to-identity risk: the SAME cusp-fold algebra (27h²=4) is independently reused across BIRCA's mood/health cusp, readout_universe's §7.23 bistability discussion, and research_universal_solver's InfoDecisionAgency_attempt decision-cusp — three sources converging on one shared form. This is exactly the pattern that invites overclaiming a single underlying mechanism; every source that discusses it already explicitly refuses that inference ('mildly suggestive parallel', 'does NOT show any special link') — the synthesis must not be the first document to cross that line the sources themselves drew.

Fabricated-citation risk on partially-verified sources: the body topic's three Coq health files (InfoHealthCuspFold_attempt.v etc.) were confirmed present as compiled .vo artifacts but NOT independently re-run (coqc/Print Assumptions) by the research pass — tier is 'unverified-model,' not Th_coqc, despite PROVENANCE.md's claim. Similarly HUMAN_AGENCY_SINGLE_TAU_C.md and AGENCY_VS_AGENCY_LIKE.md's InfoDecisionAgency_attempt content in the affect_drive topic are read/quoted but their own upstream tier claims (Th_coqc vs Dr) were not re-verified this pass. Synthesis must cite these at their stated-but-unverified status, not as settled fact.

'AI has no morality of its own' (ethics topic, verbatim quote from philosophy.md §7.22) is easy to misquote in the direction of implying the opposite once paraphrased — the misleading_passages entry for this exact quote already flags this risk; the synthesis must use the source's own suggested-fix wording or equivalent, not the bare quote in isolation.

Kant/Nietzsche-as-standard risk is narrow but real: main.tex's own Ethics (L-16) chapter contains a Cj-tier remark that the framework 'lands closer to discourse ethics than to utilitarianism/deontology' — this is the corpus's OWN conjectural remark, not an external validation exercise, but a careless synthesis sentence could read as 'the framework is validated by resembling discourse ethics,' which would violate the founder's instruction not to use any named ethical-theory tradition as a satisfaction standard.

Single-repo judgment risk: several of the strongest-sounding claims (e.g. body's PHASE_V_LIFE_AND_HEALTH block, affect_drive's 'affective weighting' term, psych_self's L_H inter-agent clause) live ONLY in research_universal_solver and are entirely uncited in readout_universe itself. The synthesis must repeatedly distinguish 'this is readout_universe's own established content' from 'this is solver-repo raw material not yet imported/synthesized into readout_universe,' per the five-way distinction rule — a drafter working quickly could flatten this distinction when writing continuous prose.

Bare 'thin' wording risk is highest in the ethics topic, which has ~8 rows tagged status_category 'absent' / tier 'Open' (arbitration between parties, authority-to-set, gaming/adversarial robustness, irreversible harm, accountability allocation, cultural-conflict tie-break, proxy representation) — each already has the required 5 parts in the coverage map, but the synthesis drafter must carry all 5 through rather than compressing to 'this is not addressed.'

Emotion-reduced-to-pathology risk is explicitly named as a live gap by the affect_drive topic's own candidate_gaps: every existing closure/repair passage in both readout_universe and BIRCA frames tension/deviation unidirectionally as something to be dissipated/rescued from, with only one weak, explicitly-disclaimed counter-example (Rescorla-Wagner). The synthesis must present this as an accurately-described one-sidedness in the existing corpus (a finding), not resolve it by inventing a 'productive tension' claim that doesn't exist in the source material — either move would violate a stated rule (fabrication vs. under-reporting the actual gap).

Cross-topic duplication during integration: the BIRCA calm-anchor/bistability/cusp-fold structural echo is documented independently (with slightly different framing and caveats) in the body, affect_drive, and psych_self topics' cross_reference_map and coverage_rows. The Integrator merging these into one combined cross-reference map risks either (a) silently choosing one topic's weaker caveat over another's stronger one, or (b) creating an apparent triple-confirmation effect (three independent-looking citations of the same underlying analogy) that reads as stronger evidence than any single source claims — the merge must flatten to one claim with the union of all caveats, not multiply perceived support.
